open_points.subject: flow composition versus unknown references
open_points.text: A05 says a function node naming a missing contract version or an operation node naming a missing binding fails proof and the version is kept; A16 says any request naming a record that does not exist is refused before the operation's own checks, never as a proof failure.
open_points.question: When a composed flow names a missing contract version or binding, is the flow version kept with a failed proof, or is composition refused with nothing kept?
options: Keep the version and return a phase-1 proof failure
Refuse composition as an unknown reference and keep nothing
open_points.default_guess: Refuse composition and keep nothing, following A16's global request rule.

open_points.subject: caller-supplied content identities
open_points.text: A01 says "A request that supplies one of these identities is refused," although implementation submission, trial, rollback and flow activation must name existing contract, implementation or flow-version identities.
open_points.question: Does this prohibition apply only when a caller asserts the identity of newly submitted content, or also when an operation uses the identity as a reference to an existing record?
options: Refuse only asserted identities for newly created content
Refuse every request field containing one of these identities
open_points.default_guess: Allow identities as references and refuse them only as caller-asserted identities of new content.

open_points.subject: flow edge ordering and identity
open_points.text: Edges are ordered and hashed by (`to_node`, `to_port`, `from_node`, `from_port`), but distinct guarded edges may have the same four fields and different guards.
open_points.question: What tie-breaker orders distinct edges with identical endpoint tuples for proof failures and canonical flow-version identity?
options: Use the guard port and canonical guard value as further keys
Use the canonical JSON of the entire edge as the final tie-breaker
Treat parallel edges with identical endpoints as malformed
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical JSON of the complete edge as the final tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: flow constant ordering and identity
open_points.text: Constants are sorted only by (`to_node`, `to_port`), while duplicate constants for one port are retained in an unproven version until phase 6 rejects them.
open_points.question: How are two constants with the same target but different values ordered for hashing and for selecting the first failure?
options: Use the constant's canonical value and class as tie-breakers
Reject duplicate targets before a flow version is kept
Preserve request order
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical JSON of the complete constant as the final tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: ProofResult failure location
open_points.text: M17 permits "the first failing edge or node," but A05 can first fail on a constant, a flow input, a flow output, or a target port with no source.
open_points.question: What exact failure locator is returned for proof failures that are neither a node nor an edge?
options: Use a tagged locator covering node, edge, constant and flow port
Always translate the failure to the affected node or edge
Return only phase and reason for such failures
open_points.default_guess: Use a tagged locator that can identify every checked item.

open_points.subject: schema validation on binding and flow ports
open_points.text: M01 says every port schema is in the supported subset, but A02 explicitly validates this only for contract ports; A05 and A08 do not state when unsupported schemas on flow or binding ports are rejected or where that failure appears.
open_points.question: When and in what order are unsupported schemas on binding ports and flow input/output ports rejected?
options: Reject them as malformed proposal or composition requests before records are kept
Keep the record and make proof fail
Validate binding schemas at proposal and flow schemas at composition, with explicit positions in each check order
open_points.default_guess: Validate binding schemas at proposal and flow schemas at composition before keeping the record.

open_points.subject: empty node identifiers
open_points.text: A05 uses the empty string as the node component of every flow input or output endpoint, but no rule forbids a FlowNode whose `node_id` is the empty string.
open_points.question: Is an empty `node_id` forbidden, or how is it distinguished from a flow endpoint in ordering and identity?
options: Forbid an empty `node_id`
Represent endpoint kind separately so an empty node identifier remains valid
open_points.default_guess: Forbid an empty `node_id`.

open_points.subject: constants targeting many ports
open_points.text: M16 says a constant is delivered to one input like any other value, while A05 applies cardinality rules only to edges and A13 says a `many` value is an array whose elements fit the port schema.
open_points.question: May a constant target a `many` input, and if so is its literal the whole array or one element to be lifted into an array?
options: Allow it only when the literal is the complete array
Forbid constants on `many` inputs
Treat the literal as one element and create a one-element array
open_points.default_guess: Allow it only as the complete array, validating every element against the port schema.

open_points.subject: guard value comparison
open_points.text: A05 and A13 say a guard is enabled when the runtime value "equals" the declared closed value, without defining equality for JSON values.
open_points.question: Is guard equality canonical-byte equality, JSON Schema enum equality, or language-native equality, especially for values such as `1` and `1.0`?
options: Compare RFC 8785 canonical bytes
Use the equality semantics of the supported JSON Schema subset
Use Python equality
open_points.default_guess: Use RFC 8785 canonical-byte equality.

open_points.subject: file-port value schemas
open_points.text: Every port has a `value_schema` and edges require equal schemas, but files are passed as bytes, function file outputs are checked only for being `bytes`, and K-10 says the kernel does not inspect file content.
open_points.question: What does a file port's `value_schema` describe, which file facts are validated against it, and which schemas are legal for file ports?
options: Require one fixed schema representing a file handle and use media type for content typing
Validate a schema against file metadata such as digest and size
Treat the schema only as an opaque compatibility declaration
open_points.default_guess: Require one fixed file schema and use media type as the file-content compatibility rule.

open_points.subject: authored trial-case input and expected-output keys
open_points.text: A04 requires input values and present expected outputs to fit their ports, but does not say whether every input must be present, whether extra keys are refused, or whether present expected outputs must cover every output port.
open_points.question: What exact key sets are required for authored trial inputs and for `expected_outputs` when that field is present?
options: Inputs must exactly match all input ports and expected outputs must exactly match all output ports
Inputs must be exact but expected outputs may be a subset
Both may be partial
open_points.default_guess: Require exact input keys and, when expected outputs are present, exact output keys.

open_points.subject: rollback eligibility
open_points.text: Rollback selects an "earlier implementation" but A04 only tests that it belongs to the current contract version and has an admitted verdict over the current corpus.
open_points.question: Does "earlier" mean any non-current implementation, one submitted before the current implementation, or only one that was previously activated?
options: Any non-current admitted implementation of the current contract version
Only an implementation submitted before the current one
Only a previously activated implementation
open_points.default_guess: Allow any non-current implementation of the current contract version with the required verdict.

open_points.subject: deterministic function execution and admission
open_points.text: K-05 calls admission deterministic and A03 requires the same implementation and input to yield the same digest, but permitted Python code can observe process IDs, thread scheduling, runtime-file metadata and other changing host facts, and timeout or resource-limit outcomes can vary with machine load.
open_points.question: What observable sources must be fixed or prohibited so repeated executions and admission verdicts are actually deterministic?
options: Prohibit or virtualize every observable nondeterministic source
Define determinism only as reuse of the first stored verdict for an implementation and corpus
Drop the deterministic-execution guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Prohibit or virtualize observable nondeterministic sources and define deterministic resource accounting.

open_points.subject: clock prohibition in the sandbox
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has no clock and A03 says every clock entry point is replaced, but A03's closed list omits available clock APIs such as `time.clock_gettime` and other timing observations.
open_points.question: Are all unlisted clock APIs forbidden by another mechanism, or are they intentionally available despite K-02?
options: Trap every clock API exposed by the pinned runtime
Allow only the explicitly listed traps and weaken the no-clock claim
Block clock system calls at the isolation boundary
open_points.default_guess: Block clock access at the isolation boundary and trap every exposed runtime API.

open_points.subject: function filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 allows "no filesystem beyond its input," while A03 permits opens anywhere in the exchange directory and the read-only runtime and gives the environment bounded scratch space.
open_points.question: May user code inspect runtime files and create arbitrary scratch files, or may only the runner access those paths for input and output exchange?
options: Permit user code to use the exchange directory and read runtime files
Permit only declared input/output files and deny all other user-code filesystem access
Permit scratch files but hide runtime files other than imports
open_points.default_guess: Permit bounded private scratch and declared inputs, while preventing arbitrary inspection of runtime files.

open_points.subject: sandbox resource accounting
open_points.text: A03 says process count and scratch space are bounded, but does not define whether the runner counts as a process, how descendants are counted, or whether scratch usage is apparent bytes, allocated blocks, current usage or peak usage.
open_points.question: What exact quantities are compared with `process_count` and `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`?
options: Count all sandbox processes including the runner and peak allocated filesystem bytes
Count only user-created child processes and current apparent file sizes
Define separate implementation-visible and supervisor overhead allowances
open_points.default_guess: Count every process inside the sandbox, including the runner, and peak allocated scratch bytes.

open_points.subject: release upgrades and existing admissions
open_points.text: A20 pins the sandbox runtime and dependencies per release, but only preserves old contract resource bounds; it does not say what happens to existing verdicts and activations when a new release changes Python, dependencies or sandbox traps.
open_points.question: After an upgrade, may an implementation admitted under the previous runtime continue serving under the new runtime without re-admission?
options: Keep and execute the old runtime for records admitted under it
Invalidate or recompute admissions before those implementations serve
Continue using existing verdicts under the new runtime
open_points.default_guess: Require re-admission under the new runtime before an existing implementation can serve.

open_points.subject: manifest revision resolution
open_points.text: The kernel reads `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` "at the configured `manifest_revision`," but no rule defines how a revision is resolved, checked out, verified or held stable during the process lifetime.
open_points.question: What concrete operation maps `manifest_location` and `manifest_revision` to immutable file bytes, and what start failure occurs when it cannot be resolved?
options: Read through a repository API at the exact commit without checkout
Require `manifest_location` already to be an immutable checkout matching the revision
Copy the selected revision into a kernel-owned snapshot at start
open_points.default_guess: Create and use a read-only snapshot of the exact revision at start.

open_points.subject: platform manifest schema
open_points.text: A08 lists selected missing fields and invalid values, but does not define the required JSON types and complete shapes of `capabilities`, capability entries, `exposed_as`, instances, required headers and related fields.
open_points.question: Which complete manifest schema is validated, and where do wrong JSON types or malformed but present structures fall in A08's first-failure order?
options: Define a complete manifest schema and validate it before the field-specific checks
Treat every unlisted malformed shape as invalid JSON
Let individual field readers report implementation-specific mismatches
open_points.default_guess: Validate a complete manifest schema first, with one ordered manifest-shape failure.

open_points.subject: read-operation idempotency metadata
open_points.text: For a `read`, A08 says `idempotency_key` is not used and not checked, while M10 and M11 still carry `idempotency_key_fields` copied from the manifest.
open_points.question: What is stored when a read capability has a missing, malformed or non-text `idempotency_key`?
options: Always store an empty field list for reads and ignore the manifest value
Validate and copy it even though reads do not use it
Require it to be `null` for reads
open_points.default_guess: Store an empty field list for reads and ignore the manifest value.

open_points.subject: base URL and declared path syntax
open_points.text: A08 accepts any absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host, and A09 concatenates it with the declared path, but neither excludes user information, an existing path, query, fragment or malformed percent escapes; the declared path also lacks a complete allowed-character grammar.
open_points.question: What exact URL and path grammar is accepted before an operation is invocable?
options: Require an origin-only base URL and an RFC 3986 path with validated percent escapes
Permit a base path but forbid user information, query and fragment
Permit all absolute URLs and rely on the HTTP client
open_points.default_guess: Require an origin-only base URL with no user information, path, query or fragment, plus a strictly validated path.

open_points.subject: multipart port names and media types
open_points.text: A09 inserts port names verbatim into quoted `Content-Disposition` parameters and media types into `Content-Type`, while A02 defines no HTTP-safe syntax for either.
open_points.question: Are unsafe characters rejected, or what exact escaping is used for quotes, backslashes, controls and non-ASCII text in multipart names, filenames and media types?
options: Restrict port names and media types to an HTTP-safe grammar
Define exact RFC-compliant escaping and encoding
Use an HTTP library's unspecified escaping
open_points.default_guess: Restrict multipart-visible names and media types to explicit safe grammars.

open_points.subject: multipart request approval
open_points.text: State 0 says approval covers the fully built request and any difference asks again, but A10 excludes the multipart boundary from both the content-type description and body description, allowing different wire bytes under the same approval.
open_points.question: Is the multipart boundary part of the exact approved request, or are requests with different boundaries intentionally equivalent?
options: Include a deterministic boundary in the approval digest
Declare boundary differences semantically equivalent despite different wire bytes
Store and reuse the exact originally generated boundary
open_points.default_guess: Generate a deterministic boundary and include it in the approved request.

open_points.subject: oversized error responses
open_points.text: A20 says a response over a ceiling is always a refusal or failure and never truncation, but A09 says 3xx, 4xx and 5xx outcomes apply whatever the body's size and that reading simply stops at the ceiling; some of those outcomes are waits rather than failures.
open_points.question: Does the response-size ceiling override an error status, or is discarded error-body overflow an explicit exception to A20?
options: Make every oversized response a contract violation
Keep the status-based outcome and declare discarded error bodies an exception
Use status-based outcomes only when the complete body is within the ceiling
open_points.default_guess: Keep the conservative effect outcome but explicitly classify and record response overflow as part of that outcome.

open_points.subject: HTTP and manifest metadata bounds
open_points.text: No ceiling bounds response headers, manifest file size or depth, base URLs, required-header values, operation entries, or credential values, although services are untrusted and A20 says every global ceiling is fixed by the release.
open_points.question: What limits apply to these inputs, and what outcomes result when they are exceeded?
options: Add release ceilings and ordered refusal or failure rules for each
Reuse `bounded_text_bytes_max` and `surface_request_bytes_max`
Rely on HTTP, JSON and filesystem libraries' limits
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit release ceilings with deterministic refusal and transport-failure mappings.

open_points.subject: resend after a direct not_applied outcome
open_points.text: A09 maps a non-read 4xx response to EffectAttempt `not_applied` and NodeExecution `operation_refused`, which A13 treats as a final failed element; A10 and M26 nevertheless say every resend after `not_applied` requires a fresh approval, while A11 only creates that resend path when an unknown attempt is resolved `not_applied`.
open_points.question: Can a direct 4xx `not_applied` attempt be retried in the same run, and if so which action changes the failed element into an approval wait?
options: Treat direct 4xx as final with no same-run resend
Turn every `not_applied` outcome into an approval wait
Add an explicit owner retry action for a `not_applied` attempt
open_points.default_guess: Treat every `not_applied` outcome as waiting for a fresh owner approval.

open_points.subject: scope of repeat detection after not_applied
open_points.text: K-08 says sending an effect again after `not_applied` needs fresh approval, while A10 defines freshness using the latest attempt of one run, node and element.
open_points.question: Does the fresh-approval requirement apply only within that element's run, or also to a later run with the same binding, inputs and idempotency key?
options: Only within the same run element
Across all runs sharing the idempotency key
Across runs only for `draft-write`, because other effect classes ask anyway
open_points.default_guess: Apply it across runs that have the same operation and idempotency key.

open_points.subject: empty mapped-node output disclosure class
open_points.text: A13 says an empty mapped output list takes the class of the list mapped over, but A07 says a function output takes the highest class of every input and an operation output takes the binding's declared class.
open_points.question: What class does each output of a mapped node over an empty list receive when other broadcast inputs have a higher class or when the node is an operation?
options: For a function use the highest class of all supplied inputs; for an operation use the binding output class
Always use the mapped list's class
Use the proof-time maximum class for every empty mapped output
open_points.default_guess: Use all input classes for a function and the declared binding output class for an operation.

open_points.subject: oversized aggregate output of a mapped node
open_points.text: A13 creates each mapped value output as one aggregate StoredValue, while A15 says an oversized produced value concludes the producing element `contract_violation`; an aggregate can exceed the ceiling although every element already succeeded, and there is no aggregate NodeExecution.
open_points.question: Which record fails when the collected list exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, and what happens to the already written successful element records?
options: Make the last element a contract violation and keep earlier element records
Write a separate aggregate NodeExecution for the mapped node
Treat the mapped node as failed without changing element records and record a separate aggregation failure
open_points.default_guess: Record a separate mapped-node aggregation failure without rewriting concluded element records.

open_points.subject: agent-name uniqueness during configuration reload
open_points.text: M27 requires unique agent names and refuses duplicate names at start, but A16 says exactly three reload checks apply and duplicate agent names are not one of them.
open_points.question: What happens when a token-file reload contains distinct tokens with the same agent name?
options: Reject the reload like an unknown token until names are unique
Allow it and treat both tokens as the same Actor
Accept only the first or last occurrence
open_points.default_guess: Reject the reload until agent names are unique.

open_points.subject: agent-name reuse over time
open_points.text: Actor identity stores only `agent_name`, while tokens may be removed and later added and no rule forbids assigning a former name to a different agent.
open_points.question: Does reusing an agent name mean the same logical Actor, or must names never be reassigned during the lifetime of the store?
options: Names are permanent identities and cannot be reassigned
Reusing a name intentionally denotes the same actor
Add a persistent actor generation or identifier
open_points.default_guess: Treat names as permanent identities and forbid reassignment.

open_points.subject: configuration reload contents and snapshot
open_points.text: A16 says the kernel re-reads "only the token list," although M28 separates `owner_token` and `agent_tokens`, and describes a hash read followed by another read when changed.
open_points.question: Does reload include the owner token and agent names and author rights, and are hashing and parsing performed from the same immutable byte snapshot?
options: Reload owner and complete agent entries from one byte snapshot
Reload only agent token strings and keep all other authentication facts from start
Reload agents but require restart for an owner-token change
open_points.default_guess: Reload the owner token and complete agent entries from one byte snapshot.

open_points.subject: configuration recovery after a failed reload
open_points.text: After a failed reload the old list is not kept and every request is refused "until a re-read passes," but the normal rule re-parses only when the file hash differs; a restored file may have the same hash as the last valid file.
open_points.question: Once reload has failed, does every later request force a full parse until one succeeds, even when the restored bytes match the previous valid hash?
options: Force a full re-read while configuration state is invalid
Restore the discarded cached list when the old hash returns
Require a different file revision before requests can recover
open_points.default_guess: Force a full read and parse on every request until one succeeds.

open_points.subject: configuration-file protection after start
open_points.text: A17 requires the configuration file to be regular, non-symlink, owner-owned and private at start, but A16 says exactly three checks apply on reload and omits all file-type, ownership and permission checks.
open_points.question: May a replaced, symlinked or newly world-readable configuration file supply live tokens after startup?
options: Recheck type, ownership, symlink status and permissions on every reload
Trust the path after the initial start checks
Refuse all live token reloads after file replacement
open_points.default_guess: Recheck all protection properties on every reload.

open_points.subject: service credential references and secret files
open_points.text: A17 refers to host-resolved secret files but gives no rules for their path resolution, symlink handling, ownership, permissions, maximum size or atomic reading.
open_points.question: What exact checks must a credential source pass before its value is accepted?
options: Apply regular-file, no-symlink, owner-only and bounded-size checks
Delegate all protection and reading semantics to a named host secret provider
Accept any readable referenced file
open_points.default_guess: Require a bounded regular file, opened without following links, owned by the kernel user and inaccessible to group or others.

open_points.subject: database and filesystem crash consistency
open_points.text: A18 says every store call is one transaction and a failed call changes nothing, while records are coordinated with separately flushed and renamed files and spool deletion; no protocol covers crashes between filesystem changes and the SQLite commit.
open_points.question: What ordering and recovery protocol keeps value files, trial fixtures, produced spool files, run endings, releases and capture records consistent across a crash?
options: Use staged files plus a database intent journal and startup reconciliation
Commit database records first and repair missing or excess files on startup
Perform filesystem changes first and remove all unreferenced files on startup
open_points.default_guess: Use staged files with durable intent records and deterministic startup reconciliation.

open_points.subject: failed-run release atomicity
open_points.text: Release must both record `released_by` and remove the spool, but a crash after deletion and before the record commit can leave an apparently unreleased run whose files are already gone.
open_points.question: After such a crash, is the run marked released during recovery, is the deletion rolled back, or may capture fail despite the run appearing unreleased?
options: Record a durable release intent before deleting and finish it on recovery
Commit release first and delete files afterward
Allow an unreleased-looking run with missing files
open_points.default_guess: Commit a durable release intent first and complete both the record and deletion during recovery.

open_points.subject: surface request serialization order
open_points.text: A18 says concurrent surface requests are handled one at a time "in the order they arrive," but no event defines arrival when requests overlap or are multiplexed.
open_points.question: What observable event establishes the total order of simultaneous requests?
options: Order when a complete validated message is enqueued
Order when the first byte is received
Let the MCP server choose an unspecified serialization order
open_points.default_guess: Order by the sequence in which complete messages enter the kernel's single request queue.

open_points.subject: data-directory privacy checks
open_points.text: A18 says the data directory and everything in it are "private to the kernel's user" and startup refuses otherwise, without specifying ownership, allowed mode bits or which file types are valid.
open_points.question: What exact owner, permission and file-type predicates are checked for the directory and each contained object?
options: Require kernel-user ownership and no group or other permissions on every object
Check only the root directory
Use exact modes per object type
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership, no group or other permission bits, and expected regular-file or directory types throughout.

open_points.subject: personal-data disclosure through derived observations
open_points.text: K-14 says the owner alone reads personal data and agents receive only digest and class, but an agent-written function can branch on personal input and reveal bits through known output digests, success or failure, resource usage, output shape or repeated trials.
open_points.question: Is the requirement only syntactic non-return of payload bytes, or must the kernel prevent an agent from inferring personal data through function-controlled observations?
options: The guarantee is only syntactic redaction and such inference is accepted
Hide content digests and execution side channels for personal-data executions
Forbid agent-written functions from receiving personal data
open_points.default_guess: Treat the stated digest-and-class rule as syntactic disclosure only unless the product strengthens the threat model.

open_points.subject: authentication-token handling outside responses
open_points.text: A16 forbids tokens in responses, while A17's stronger prohibition on logs, records and process arguments names service credentials but not owner or agent tokens.
open_points.question: May authentication tokens appear in logs, traces, stored request data, failure details or process arguments?
options: Forbid them everywhere outside protected configuration and in-memory comparison
Forbid only responses and traces
Apply the service-credential rule to all tokens
open_points.default_guess: Apply the service-credential prohibition to owner and agent tokens as well.
